deep_analysis.executive_intro:
The FTSE screen is broadly cautious: 144 names sit on Hold versus 61 actionable Buys (20 Strong Buy, 41 Buy) and 43 Avoids. Among the highest-conviction names, Industrials dominate—three of five top candidates (FirstGroup, ME Group, Morgan Sindall)—with Healthcare (Hikma) and Communication Services (ITV) rounding out the list. All five pass every model family (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) and carry persistent 13-week signals, but several were downgraded from Strong Buy to Buy by FCF-basis overlays. A central data limitation is free-cash-flow definition divergence: filing, screen TTM, and company-adjusted FCF figures disagree materially across most top picks, which can distort yield-dependent model passes and dividend-coverage readings.

**FGP.L (FirstGroup plc)** — Flagged Strong Buy on 15/22 models (composite 89%, sector-relative 87%) with passes across Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG (PEG 0.55, growth 16%), Piotroski F-Score (8/9), and Composite Value; key metrics are P/E 8.8, P/B 1.4, yield 4.1%, ROE 16.7%, and filing D/E 19%. Failures include Financial Health (weak liquidity, current ratio 0.73), Economic Moat, and Graham Defensive. Three of five top picks are Industrials, adding sector concentration if building a basket. **Verdict: watchlist** — strong quantitative profile but FCF basis mismatch (filing £362.6M vs screen TTM £302.8M vs company-adj £113.5M) and adjusted signal downgraded to Buy warrant reconciling cash-flow definitions before sizing.

**HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals)** — Strong Buy on 11/22 models (composite 81%, sector-relative 91%) via Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, and Financial Health; metrics include P/E 12.3, P/B 1.8, yield 4.0%, ROE 15.4%, D/E 77%. Notable failures: FCF Yield (3.6% below 5% threshold), Lynch PEG (growth 1.7%, PEG 7.02), Piotroski F-Score (6/9), Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion), and Economic Moat. Healthcare is the sole representative among top picks, so no sector-cluster risk here. **Verdict: watchlist** — attractive sector-relative score and balance-sheet pass, but statutory FCF dividend coverage of 0.64× versus management 1.31× and adjusted signal of Buy argue for patience until cash conversion clarity improves.

**MEGP.L (ME Group International)** — Strong Buy on 15/22 models (composite 82%, sector-relative 88%) including Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Economic Moat (ROE 28.2%, margin 17.6%), High Dividend Yield (6.7%), Magic Formula, and Financial Health; P/E 8.3, P/B 2.4, D/E 28%. Failures: Lynch PEG (filing-core growth 0.4%, model PEG 22.87), Piotroski F-Score (6/9), and Earnings Quality; interim-quality overlay flagged declining interim EPS and net FCF/dividend coverage below 1.0× (0.84× statutory). Adds to Industrials concentration alongside FGP.L and MGNS.L. **Verdict: watchlist** — compelling cheapness and moat pass, but timing signal is "wait," earnings growth basis diverges >300 bps (statutory 4.5% vs filing core 0.4%), and adjusted signal is Buy.

**ITV.L (ITV plc)** — Strong Buy on 15/22 models (composite 82%, sector-relative 87%) with Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield (7.1%), Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG (PEG 0.52, growth 23%), High Dividend Yield (7.0%), Dreman Contrarian, Earnings Quality, and Financial Health; P/E 11.8, P/B 1.5, ROE 13.5%, D/E 52%. Failures include Buffett Quality (thin margins), Economic Moat, and a weak Piotroski F-Score (3/9). Only Communication Services name in the top five. **Verdict: accumulate** — only top candidate with favourable timing (RSI 42, below 200-day MA, timing score 0.75) and statutory FCF dividend coverage at 1.0×, though adjusted signal remains Buy pending FCF basis reconciliation (£148M filing vs £211.9M screen TTM vs £187M company-adj).

**MGNS.L (Morgan Sindall Group)** — Highest model pass count at 16/22 (composite 80%, sector-relative 82%) with Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield (8.5%), Lynch PEG (PEG 0.56, growth 19.6%), Buffett Quality, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Earnings Quality, and Financial Health; P/E 11.0, P/B 2.6, yield 3.9%, ROE 26.1%, D/E 18%, FCF dividend coverage 2.59×. Failures: Graham Defensive, Economic Moat (ROA/margins), and High Dividend Yield. Highest conviction score (81%) and only top pick retaining adjusted Strong Buy; third Industrials name. **Verdict: accumulate** — cleanest profile among top picks with strong F-Score, earnings growth, and no FCF definition divergence flag, though construction cyclicality sits outside the screen.

- **FGP.L:** Public-transport operator exposed to franchise renewal, regulatory fare caps, and government funding cycles—not modelled. Current ratio 0.73 and Yahoo D/E 161% (vs filing-adjusted £137.7m net debt) suggest lease/accounting complexity the screen partially overrides; pension deficit status is an open question.
- **HIK.L:** Generic-drug pricing pressure, FDA/regulatory inspection risk, and patent-cliff exposure are not captured. Statutory FCF dividend coverage 0.64× raises dividend sustainability questions; leverage D/E 77% flagged in Economic Moat and Buffett Quality failures.
- **MEGP.L:** Photo-booth/vending-machine business is inherently discretionary and location-dependent; cyclical consumer-spending sensitivity not flagged by screen. Interim EPS decline and net FCF coverage 0.84× below dividend suggest near-term payout strain; earnings growth basis divergence (>300 bps) is unresolved.
- **ITV.L:** Structural advertising cyclicality, streaming competition, and Ofcom/regulatory oversight on broadcasting are absent from quantitative filters. Piotroski F-Score 3/9 signals deteriorating fundamentals trend; 7.0% yield may embed market scepticism on durability—governance and pension obligations are open questions (not in JSON).
- **MGNS.L:** UK construction and regeneration is highly cyclical; order-book concentration and contract-risk provisions are not screened. Thin margins flagged in Quality Value and Buffett Quality; current ratio 1.23 below Graham Defensive threshold. Pension deficit and project-liability exposure require manual review.

documents.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
documents.executive_summary:
Hikma is a FTSE 100 generics and specialty pharmaceutical group spanning Injectables, Branded MENA, and US Hikma Rx, reporting in USD. The quantitative screen rates it **Strong Buy** (11/22 models, 81% composite, all five factor families passed) on a ~12× P/E, 1.8× P/B, ~4% yield and 15% ROE — cheap versus a diversified, FDA-inspected manufacturing footprint. FY2025 filings show revenue and core profit growth, but statutory free cash flow fell sharply to **$119m** (operating cash **$436m** less elevated capex and **$186m** legal settlements), creating a central debate on cash conversion and dividend durability. H1 2026 interim results were stronger (core operating profit **+9%**), and management has reiterated FY2026 guidance, but Injectables margins remain under pressure and net debt has risen. The value case rests on earnings power and capital return; the bear case on low reported growth, FCF definition divergence, and segment/regulatory risk.

---
documents.investment_thesis:
The screen’s **Strong Buy** signal is well supported on classical value metrics: P/E 12.3, P/B 1.85, dividend yield ~4%, debt/equity 77%, current ratio 1.8, and passes across Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value and Financial Health. Conviction is **73%**, persistent for 13 weeks with stable trend — unusually consistent for healthcare.

Business quality aligns with several passes. FY2025 core revenue grew **6%** to **$3,349m**; core operating profit **+3%** to **$741m** (22.1% margin); Branded grew core operating profit **+19%**. The group operates **13 US FDA-inspected plants**, launched 84 products in 2025, and received **BBB** upgrades from S&P and Fitch. Return on average invested capital was **16.0%**. Capital return is active: FY2025 total dividend **84 cents** (+5%), a **$250m** buyback (completed second tranche Aug 2026 per news), and H1 2026 interim dividend **38 cents** (+6%).

Where the screen and business diverge explains failed models and the overlay caution. Statutory EPS growth is only **~1.7%**, failing Lynch PEG (PEG ~7.0) and Economic Moat screens. FCF Yield fails (3.6% vs 5% threshold): filing-aligned FCF **$119m** vs prior-year **$329m**, with statutory OCF-minus-capex dividend cover **0.64×** vs management-adjusted **1.31×** — a flagged definition divergence. Piotroski F-Score is **6/9** (leverage not declining; gross margin and asset turnover not improving). For a value investor, Hikma offers a **quality compounder trading at a cyclical/generic discount** after a difficult 2023 impairment year and Feb 2026 guidance reset, with H1 2026 suggesting operational recovery — but not a deep-value net-net or high-FCF-yield compounder without further verification of normalised cash generation.

---
documents.financial_review:
*Primary: FY2025 press release (`ir_0e40d9707e30c3b7.txt`); H1 2026 (`5f26e81d036b3596.txt`); Apr 2026 trading update (`94eb1f8d38a51fa6.txt`); refetched CH 2025 annual extract (`ch_05557934_MzUxODk1NDgyN2FkaXF6a2N4.txt`) for highlight corroboration. Yahoo (`financials_annual.json`) for multi-year balance-sheet series only.*

**FY2025:** Revenue $3,349m (+7%); core OP $741m (+3%); reported OP $542m (−11%, $186m settlement cash); dividend 84¢ (+5%). Cash generated $560m → net OCF $436m → statutory FCF $119m after capex $317m; dividend cover 0.64× statutory / 1.31× management. Net debt/core EBITDA 1.6×. CH 2025 refetch corroborates headline figures.

**H1 2026:** Revenue $1,728m (+4%); core OP $405m (+9%); OCF $214m (+33%); interim dividend 38¢ (+6%). Net debt $1,694m; leverage 1.9×. Branded +15%; Injectables flat, core profit −8%; 503B compounding wind-down. $227m of $250m buyback done. FY2026 guidance reiterated.

**Trend (Yahoo fallback):** FCF $360m→$119m (2022–25). Net debt $920m→$1,334m (2023–25).

**Gaps:** Refetched CH bodies add narrative corroboration but not principal-risks register (p. 82) or debt-maturity notes. No patent-expiry schedule. Yahoo quarterly cashflow empty — ignore screen TTM FCF $14.4m.

**Regulatory/FDA — evidenced (partially closed).** CH 2024: “regularly inspected by the US FDA.” 503B wind-down reduces one line. CH 2025 refetch indexes risk section but supplies no principal-risk prose. Open: FDA 483/warning-letter inventory.

**Patent/IP — evidenced (partially closed).** $186m antitrust settlement; Amarin litigation ongoing. Open: no patent-cliff calendar.

**Customer concentration — evidenced.** Three US wholesalers ≥10% each (~33% combined, FY2025 Note 3).

**Cash/dividend — evidenced (partially closed).** Statutory 0.64× cover confirmed; H1 OCF recovery supportive; full-year unproven at 1.9× leverage with buyback.

**Leverage — evidenced (partially closed).** 1.6×→1.9× net debt/EBITDA; D/E 77% drives Economic Moat fail; covenants suspended at BBB. Open: debt maturity schedule.

documents.name: ME Group International plc
documents.executive_summary: ME Group International plc operates a global estate of ~49,000 instant-service vending machines, led by Photo.ME photobooths and the fast-growing Wash.ME laundry franchise. The quantitative screen rates MEGP.L as a strong buy on cheapness (P/E ~8.3, yield ~6.7%), quality (ROE ~28%), and dividend metrics, with 15 of 22 models passing across all five factor families. The valuation hook is a cash-generative, net-cash business trading at a deep earnings and FCF yield while pivoting mix toward higher-return laundry. The central debate is whether laundry expansion and capital returns offset photobooth regulatory pressure (notably Germany), a cyclical April slowdown in France, FY26 profit guidance of £69–74m (below FY25’s record £78.2m PBT), and accounting restatements plus an audit delay that unsettled governance perceptions earlier in 2026.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, ME Group offers a rare combination in UK mid-caps: dominant niche franchises, high EBITDA margins (~38% in FY25), predictable vending cash flows, and a balance sheet that remains net-cash positive despite heavy growth capex. The screen’s strong-buy signal (composite 82%, sector-relative 88%, conviction 72%, persistent 13 weeks) is underpinned by passes in cheapness (Graham Enterprising, earnings yield, FCF yield, low P/E + high yield), quality (Buffett Quality, economic moat — the only peer in the screen set to pass moat), dividend (high yield, dividend growth), GARP (Neff PEGY), and risk (financial health). Debt/equity of ~28% and a current ratio of ~1.5x support the risk bucket.

Business quality aligns with the screen rather than contradicting it. FY25 (RNS, 23 March 2026) delivered record PBT of £78.2m on revenue of £315.4m; laundry revenue rose 17.3% to £112.4m and now contributes 46.1% of group EBITDA, diversifying away from a mature photobooth estate. Management targets >1,300 laundry installations in FY26, renewed multi-year SNCF and RATP contracts (>£9m revenue combined), and the largest-ever UK laundry partnership with ASDA (ambition up to ~700 machines). Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly: total FY25 dividend of 8.64p (+9.5%, ~58% of EPS), a £18m buyback launched post-results, and a stated policy to pay >55% of profit after tax.

The screen’s adjusted signal is “buy” with timing “wait” — appropriate given interim softness, FCF definition divergence (statutory OCF−capex dividend coverage 0.84× vs management-adjusted 1.68×), and earnings-growth basis divergence (statutory EPS +4.5% vs filing core ~0.4%). The value case rests on laundry compounding and capital return at ~8× earnings, not on re-acceleration of photobooth revenue.
documents.financial_review:
Primary sources: RNS annual (23 Mar 2026), trading update (1 Jun 2026), interim (13 Jul 2026); refetched CH FY25 (`ch_00735438_MzUxODY0NzMxMGFkaXF6a2N4.txt`); FY25 annual report (`ir_55af4b8f27e3dd6f.txt`); IR presentation bridge (`ir_presentation_metrics.json`). Yahoo used only for Normalized Income and statutory OCF reconciliation.

**FY25:** Revenue £315.4m (+2.4%); EBITDA £120.4m (+5.4%); PBT £78.2m (+6.5%); diluted EPS 14.91p (+4.5%); cash generated from operations £115.5m; capex £65.6m; net cash £26.5m; dividend 8.64p (+9.5%). Wash.ME +17.3%; Photo.ME −4.0%. Dividend cover ~1.68× (filing cash-generated−capex) vs 0.84× (statutory OCF−capex £25.2m). CH FY25 extract corroborates all headline figures. Post year-end: €30m five-year BNP Paribas loan (note 32). Covenants comfortably met FY25/FY24 (note 16).

**H1 FY26:** Revenue £154.3m (+0.3%); EBITDA £57.0m (+7.1%); PBT £32.7m (−3.8%); diluted EPS 6.48p (−3.9%); cash generated £38.7m; capex £33.9m; net cash £7.5m; interim dividend cut to 3.60p. ~£4.8m pre-dividend headroom on cash-generated−capex basis.

**Trend:** Five-year diluted EPS 5.72p (2021) → 14.91p (2025) per annual report note 33 — screen 0.4% “core” growth misrepresents filing EPS trajectory. FY26 PBT £69–74m implies earnings step-down. Gaps: H1 IR FCF bridge absent; covenant headroom at Apr 2026 not quantified; CH OCR thin on principal risks.
documents.risks_and_flags:
**Evidenced:** Regulatory photobooth exposure (Germany). Cyclical/consumer sensitivity in interim risks and June trading update. Dividend strain at statutory FCF basis; H1 interim cut. Governance noise (audit delay, failed strategic review). Accounting restatements; earnings-growth screen flag is Yahoo Normalized Income vs diluted EPS, not filing adjusted EPS. FY25 covenant compliance comfortable; new €30m loan adds leverage and covenant tests.

**Still open:** Covenant headroom at H1 net cash £7.5m not quantified. ASDA concentration unproven at scale.

documents.name: ITV plc
documents.executive_summary: ITV plc screens as a strong buy on cheapness (P/E 11.8, yield 7.0%), cash generation, and dividend metrics, against a business that is pivoting from integrated broadcaster–producer to a pure-play ITV Studios plus a pending £950m cash return from the Sky M&E sale. The valuation hook is a depressed share price trading below its 200-day moving average, with a near-term catalyst path via buybacks and, from H2 2027, a large capital return — but the post-deal earnings base will be materially smaller and more production-cycle dependent. The central debate is whether headline multiples on today’s consolidated accounts understate or overstate value once M&E is carved out, regulatory approval is secured, and statutory free cash flow (filings: £148m FY2025) proves adequate to sustain the dividend through transition.
documents.investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen passes all five metric families — cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk — with 15 of 22 models clearing, including Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Lynch PEG (~0.52 on 23% earnings growth), High Dividend Yield, and Financial Health. At P/E 11.8, P/B 1.5, debt/equity 52%, and ROE 13.5%, ITV presents as a contrarian UK media value name with an income overlay, reinforced by 13 weeks at strong-buy signal and an “accumulate” timing overlay (RSI ~42, price slightly below the 200-day MA).

Business quality is mixed but directionally improving on the strategic pivot. FY2025 RNS results show external revenue up 1% to £3,511m despite a 5% decline in total advertising revenue, with ITV Studios external revenue +10% and digital revenues +10% to £614m offsetting linear weakness. ITVX viewing (+16%) and management’s ITVX payback narrative support the “More than TV” execution story. The July 2026 Sky transaction (up to £1.6bn for M&E; ~£950m / 25p per share net return to shareholders) crystallises value trapped in the broadcast arm and leaves a listed global content business underpinned by a £2.1bn minimum content supply agreement (2028–2032).

For a value investor, the screen’s strong-buy signal is grounded in real cash returns (5.0p ordinary dividend FY2025; £100m buyback announced H1 2026), moderate leverage (net debt/EBITDA 1.0x per filings), and a PEG well below 1. Failed screens (Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, Piotroski F-Score 3/9) correctly flag that this is not a wide-moat compounder — it is a transition story bought on yield, asset value, and event-driven upside rather than pristine quality metrics.

post_run_review.executive_summary: This run screened 248 names with 61 buy-tier signals (20 Strong Buy, 41 Buy) against 144 Holds and 43 Avoids—a cautious distribution dominated by Hold. Buy-tier filing ingest is broadly healthy (no tickers in `thin_filing_tickers`; 72–132 filings with body for most coverage rows), and 13 deep memos all grade “strong” with `research_verdict: accumulate`. The systemic weakness blocking conviction is not missing memo files but inconsistent cash-flow and earnings metadata: filing, screen TTM, and company-adjusted FCF diverge materially across top picks, driving FCF-basis overlays that downgrade four of five headline names from Strong Buy to Buy. Gap-fill on HIK.L, MEGP.L, and ITV.L produced six partially resolved questions (pricing/regulatory risk, EPS growth basis, dividend durability) but no closed items. Learning-path integrity shows wiring is complete (59/59 buy-tier and 19/19 Strong Buy wired to committed verdicts), yet the only system flag—medium-severity `observe_clock_stale` on sp500—shows green ingest/ops counters can mask a stale learning clock elsewhere. Top-pick conviction should stay on watchlist except ITV.L (accumulate in deep analysis); FCF reconciliation and structured risk-note ingest must land before sizing FGP.L, HIK.L, or MEGP.L.

human_tasks_checklist.title: Human tasks checklist
human_tasks_checklist.summary: Manual gates for the learning loop, knob calibration, and promotion decisions. Automated weekday runs are listed for context — verify, do not duplicate. Cadence map: docs/ops/ops-review-cadence.md.

tasks.title: Spot-check learning tracks after paper-auto
tasks.summary: Confirm weekday CI acted; on Automation tab compare AI judgment excess vs ^FTSE, rules control, and competing calibrated shadow knobs.

tasks.title: Paper-auto + decision-review apply
tasks.summary: Runs all learning tracks (including competing calibrated shadows), refreshes overlay, appends rebalance_log, applies clamped knobs when history is thick. Shadows are observe-only (no --apply); endurance ledger refreshes after review.

tasks.title: GHA secret hygiene scan
tasks.summary: Daily Actions scan for public-repo workflow_run secret-exposure patterns. Skips when no main merges / workflow touches in the last 36h; always runs on PRs that change workflows. Failures open a supervised engineering task.

tasks.title: Read analysis review synthesis
tasks.summary: After analysis-review (~10:35 UTC), read analysis_review.md for backward metrics, proposed experiments, ingest trials, and the observe-only buy-tier chart-outcome mix (well timed / giveback / no terrible).

tasks.title: Review knob calibration priors
tasks.summary: Inspect knob_calibration_priors.json: ranking_mode, ready_for_shadow_bootstrap, bootstrap_priors, confidence, score_gap_vs_runner_up, and winner/loser catch rates.

tasks.title: Review unified experiment assessment
tasks.summary: Read experiment_assessment.json for continue/fail/recommend rows. After the 2026-09-03 human pass, task recommends should be empty: u4 and exit-shadow are watch, buffered-hold and IMB.L are done, scoring is on the engineering queue. Do not reopen cancelled N58/N59 knob rows. Drill into calibration_shadow_endurance.json for shadow detail.

tasks.title: Compare calibrated shadows vs primary AI judgment
tasks.summary: On Automation tab, compare forward marks for ai_judgment vs competing calibrated shadows before promoting any prior.

tasks.title: Promote knob priors only when gates pass
tasks.summary: Do not edit ai_judgment config until a shadow is surviving, ready_for_priors/score gap look sound, and confidence is acceptable. Survivors are starting priors for refinement — never auto-apply. Stress-book (3%) excess vs ^FTSE alone is not sufficient — see fair-cost gate.

tasks.title: Require fair-cost view before treating excess as deployable
tasks.summary: Keep 3% stress books as the defensive/churn lab. Before promoting knobs or calling primary 'beating the market', check ftse-trading-costs assess and/or fair-cost warm-start shadows. Promote only when fair excess beats ^FTSE and the fair rules control (or explicitly accept stress-only churn wins).

tasks.title: Review Suite B fair-cost lab vs stress Suite A
tasks.summary: Confirm ai_judgment_fair / rules_fair are marking under T212-shaped costs, endurance_zero_datum is set, and decision-review --suite B applies stay suite-local. Do not flip primary off 3% (N48) until B excess beats ^FTSE and fair rules control with a thick forward window.

tasks.title: Spawn Suite B twins only for recommend experiments
tasks.summary: If experiment_assessment has recommend calibration/exclusion/experimental tracks, dry-run then optionally apply ftse-trading-costs spawn-fair-twins (max 2). Never auto-fork every shadow (N53). Zero recommend rows is a no-op.

tasks.title: Review entry DCA cadence when overlay readiness fires
tasks.summary: If learning_tracks_entry_dca shows ready_for_cadence_analysis, read leading cadence, mean de-risk vs lump-sum, and model_independent_hint before changing starter fraction or proposing a DCA-executing track. Observe-only; do not auto-apply.

tasks.title: Review in-portfolio hypothesis integrity when losers breach tolerance
tasks.summary: If learning_tracks_hypothesis_integrity shows within_tolerance=false, broken_loser_count>0, or selection_feedback_flags, read track hypothesis_integrity.md. Prefer thesis-broken rotation over crude stops; do not auto-apply exit knobs.

tasks.title: Triage analysis_tasks experiments

tasks.title: Exclusion ladder shadow spawn gate
tasks.summary: If exclusion_ladder_replay readiness.ready_for_shadow_spawn is true, run ftse-exclusion-ladder-replay spawn-shadow manually. Never auto-spawn.

tasks.title: Triage paper-learning and learning-director tasks

Sprint ≤4×/day × 24; maintenance ≤4×/day × 62. GitHub schedule alone is best-effort.

tasks.title: Rotate CURSOR_API_KEY after suspected exposure

Prefer main branch protection so a stolen GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push exfil workflows.

tasks.title: Register daily GHA secret-hygiene cron on cron-job.org

tasks.title: Sync valid Cursor API key into GitHub Actions secrets
tasks.summary: When ftse-verify-key --key-source legacy fails but --key-source v2 succeeds (or GHA agent jobs 401): copy the valid User API key into GitHub Actions secrets CURSOR_API_KEY_V2 and CURSOR_API_KEY. Workflows prefer V2 via secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY_V2 || secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY. Cloud secrets alone do not feed Actions.

tasks.title: Review open ingest deviations and reprocess if needed
tasks.summary: When Automation → Ingest deviations shows open rows (IR exhausted or weekday cap with leftover IWB), inspect the ticker. Approve writes a 7-day intensive pin for the next euro slot; dismiss closes the row for 7 days. Do not auto-replace IR URLs — that stays a judged allowlist edit.

H1 leaves ~£4.8m before £14.5m dividends. The >300 bps flag is not an RNS metric: no “adjusted EPS” in 67 bodies; screen 0.4% = Yahoo Normalized Income YoY (~0.36%); filing diluted EPS +4.5% (14.91p vs 14.27p, confirmed in CH extract and annual report note 33). Screen cyclical overlay remains off — a scoring gap, not an evidence gap.
